result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: Section 337 sets a four-year limit for an action on a contract, obligation or liability founded on a written instrument.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The post-sale proviso is outside the stated scope.

claims.claim: The four-year rule is subject to the Section 336a exception.
Once the Section 337 period has run, a person may not sue to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.

claims.claim: The same bar applies to initiating arbitration or another legal proceeding to collect the debt.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt.

claims.claim: The Section 337 period can be extended only under Section 360.
claims.quote: The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.

claims.claim: An acknowledgment or promise offered as evidence of a new or continuing contract to take the case outside the time-limit statutes must be in a writing signed by the party to be charged, subject to the stated note-payment proviso.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby,

claims.claim: The payment proviso covers principal or interest payments on a promissory note made by the party to be charged.
claims.quote: any payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged shall be deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract

claims.claim: Such a payment can start a new period for an action on the note.
claims.quote: as any such payment is made, the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note, and to start the running of a new period of time

claims.claim: Such a payment by itself does not revive an already barred cause of action.
claims.quote: but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.

claims.claim: An answer must state any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.quote:
(b) The answer to a complaint shall contain:
(1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
(2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.

claims.claim: Section 337 itself does not specify when the period begins for an ordinary written-contract claim.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: For this claim, subsection (a) states a duration, not a starting event. The timing language elsewhere in the section addresses different claims.

result.summary: Each claim is supported within the stated unsecured written-contract scope. The draft distinguishes restarting a period on a promissory note from reviving an already barred claim.
